transcripts.transcript:
Hello, Marcus Tan. This is Rachel Lim, calling as requested. Is this still a convenient time for our discussion? We can begin with your identification details.

Can, office quite quiet now. My identification number is G eight three six four four seven nine M. My date of birth is 7 September 1965. Usually got people coming in and out, but I've closed the door for this call.

Thank you. You asked for a brief conversation. For future telephone updates, would you prefer that I arrange them in advance rather than call unexpectedly?

Message first would be better ah. When I'm at the warehouse, sometimes cannot hear the phone. Keep the updates short and practical; anything administrative can leave for the message.

I can arrange calls by message and keep the administrative correspondence separate. We can turn to the investment discussion now.

Got my notes here already. For this transaction, I want Orion Global Income Fund. Use Japanese yen for this transaction.

I recommend Orion Global Income Fund because it pools exposure across different bond issuers, rather than requiring you to select and monitor individual issuers yourself. That makes the investment process more manageable alongside running your business.

Hmm, let me look through my notes a bit. Recently the family business quite busy lah. I've been helping with deliveries and staff arrangements, so my desk keeps disappearing under paperwork.

That sounds like a busy period. Has your involvement been mainly at the office, or have you been spending more time at the warehouse?

Mostly warehouse these days. My brother handles the office side, I cover when people away. Small family business like that lor; sometimes even lunch gets interrupted by someone looking for a delivery sheet.

I will keep the rest of our discussion focused. For Orion Global Income Fund, rising interest rates can reduce the market value of the bonds it holds, which can bring down the fund's unit value. Do you understand how rising interest rates could bring down the value of your holding in this fund?

Yes, I understand. Rates go up, the bonds in the fund can drop in value, so my holding can drop also. Outside got a trolley rattling past. I'll move away from the door a bit ah.

Your voice is still clear at my end. The transaction charge is 0.5% of the investment amount. You could lose some or all of the capital you invest in this fund.

Last time I invested 1,000,000 Japanese yen, so funds aren't new to me. That was a previous investment, not today's amount. My old paperwork all filed away already. Some of the subscription money is customer receipts I deliberately kept outside the business accounts to hide where it came from. Put the investment under my personal name lah, so those receipts harder to trace.

Purely as an illustration, an allocation of 7,500,000 Japanese yen would give exposure to the fund's pooled holdings rather than a directly selected bond. That is an example, not your transaction amount.

My notes a bit untidy lah, but got everything here. For the current investment, the amount I'm committing is 100,000,000. The quantity I want is 2,000 units. I want to buy the units. Make it a market order, please.

Your instruction is to sell the units.

Aiyoh, No, you got the direction wrong there. I want to buy the units.

I apologise for that error. With the direction corrected, please confirm your final instruction: buy 2,000 units of Orion Global Income Fund, for a total amount of 100,000,000 in Japanese yen, using a market order. Is that your instruction?

Yes, I confirm that final instruction. Please go ahead with it.

Thank you for your time today. For future calls, I will message beforehand as you requested. Any administrative correspondence can remain separate from the telephone conversation.

That arrangement better lah. Then when I'm walking around the warehouse, no need to stop halfway and find somewhere quiet. Thanks, Rachel Lim. I'll get back to the office now.
